newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt share prices ease before holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: Egypt share prices ease before holiday weekend.

text.p: Egyptian share prices eased again on Wednesday, before a long weekend, to its lowest level so far this month, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) report showed.
The bourse will be closed for a holiday on Thursday.
The CMA all-share index shed 1.53 points to close at 344.32 points in above-average trade of 64.9 million pounds ($19 million).
"The market will take up in September-October, after the holiday season," said Mohammad Abdallah, Intercapital managing director. "It's the main reason behind this decline."

Trade was swollen by the sale of another tranche of Arab Cotton Ginning. The state further reduced its 37.35 percent stake in the firm by selling 300,000 shares to the public at 60 pounds a share, the report said. The share ended unchanged.
It had sold a total 52.65 percent of the ginnery to private investors last year. The remaining ten percent is held by the firm's workers.
Suez Cement was the most active share on the market, excluding the ginnery. "This activity is normal before dividend distribution," Abdullah said.
The firm said on Wednesday it would pay out a 4.50 pound dividend per share for the calendar 1996. The dividend in 1995 was 5.20 pounds.

In the milling sector, Alexandria Flour Mills was still witnessing a selling spree, which has pushed the share price to below the offer price of 82.5 pounds. The offer earlier this month was almost 20 times oversubscribed.
The share fell 1.34 pounds to close at 78.61, when equity worth 1.3 million was traded.
"It's a funny attitude. It's a snow ball effect," said Abdullah. "The firm is the best among millers, with P/E of less than six."
Central and West Delta Flour Mills was traded in relatively high volume of 2.2 million pounds. The share shed 2.4 pounds to 76.1 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms fell marginally to 471.31 points from 471.38 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 254.71 from 256.39 points.
Half of all 88 traded shares eased, while 14 rose and 30 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
